title: Optimal deterministic price of obligatory testing
formal: Determine R_det=inf_A sup_I cost_A(I)/OPT(I) for deterministic obligatory-test scheduling with arbitrary positive test durations.
definitions: There are n≥1 labeled jobs available at time zero on one unit-speed machine. Job j requires a test of known duration t_j>0 followed, at some possibly later time, by processing of duration p_j≥0. Only completion of its test reveals p_j. Both operations are nonpreemptive, occupy the same machine and cannot overlap any other operation. Other jobs may be tested or processed between the two operations of j. The scheduler initially knows n and all t_j, but has no upper bounds or prior distributions for p_j. All durations are real, operations of zero processing duration complete immediately when scheduled, and arbitrary history-dependent policies are allowed with no computational restriction. C_j is the completion time of the processing operation and cost is ∑_j C_j. OPT knows all p_j in advance but must execute every test and obey the same single-machine and precedence constraints. No additive competitive term is allowed. The infimum is over deterministic policies that work for every n; the supremum is over all finite instances. Positive test durations ensure OPT>0. The adversary may choose processing times after seeing a deterministic policy, but each input assigns a fixed duration to every job.
answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute distance from the defined optimal ratio is at most 1/100. Certified upper and lower bounds with gap at most 1/50 qualify via their midpoint. Bounds must cover all instances and all competing policies as quantified; attaining the infimum or supremum is not required.
context: The arbitrary-test result gives a 1.861 upper bound, while uniform test durations are a separately treated restriction.
why: The problem quantifies the cost of acquiring information before scheduling work.

import_provenance.original_title: The optimal deterministic price of obligatory testing
import_provenance.original_statement: What is the optimal deterministic competitive ratio for minimizing total completion time on one machine when all jobs are initially present, each requires a known-duration test, and its processing time is revealed only by that test? Tests and processing operations are individually nonpreemptive; the general-test-time gap is between √2 and 1.861.

source_spot_check.finding: Abstract confirms the all-jobs-present obligatory-testing model and distinct general/uniform test durations.

sentences: Every job must first be tested on the same machine that processes it.
The processing duration is revealed only after the test.
Test and execution may be separated by work on other jobs.
The objective is the sum of processing completion times.
The target optimizes the deterministic ratio over unequal positive test durations.
